definitions.explanation: Short grass grown as ground cover, or a lawn made of such grass. Commonly refers to both the grass itself and the area it covers.

examples.japanese: {庭|にわ}に{芝生|しばふ}を{張|は}った。
examples.english: We laid turf in the garden.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもたちが{芝生|しばふ}の{上|うえ}で{裸足|はだし}で{走|はし}り{回|まわ}っている。
examples.english: The children are running around barefoot on the lawn.

notes:
Refers to lawn grass or turf. The compound {芝生|しばふ} (lawn, grass field) is more common in everyday conversation than {芝|しば} alone. {芝|しば} by itself appears more often in compounds or when talking about the grass material.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {芝|しば}を{刈|か}る — to mow the lawn
- {芝生|しばふ} — lawn, grass
- {芝生|しばふ}に{入|はい}るな — keep off the grass
- {人工芝|じんこうしば} — artificial turf
- {天然芝|てんねんしば} — natural turf/grass
- {芝|しば}を{張|は}る — to lay turf

RELATED TERMS:
- {芝生|しばふ} — lawn (the most common everyday form)
- {芝刈|しばか}り{機|き} — lawn mower
- {芝居|しばい} — play, theater (originally performed on grass-covered areas; now unrelated to grass)

NOTE ON {芝居|しばい}:
The word {芝居|しばい} (theater, play) historically derives from {芝|しば} because audiences once sat on the grass to watch performances, but in modern Japanese these words are completely unrelated in meaning.
